designation: IN THE COURT OF DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE
jurisdictionNote: District-level criminal and civil courts in Assam, governed by the Bengal, Agra and Assam Civil Courts Act, 1887 read with the Assam Civil Courts (Amendment) Act and the Practice Directions of the Gauhati High Court. Sessions courts try offences punishable with imprisonment exceeding 7 years. Following the 2015–2022 reorganisations, Assam presently comprises 35 revenue districts (with Bajali, Tamulpur, etc. carved from existing parent districts). The subordinate judiciary is supervised by the Gauhati High Court (principal seat, Guwahati). Assamese and English are the principal languages of pleading under the Assam Official Language Act, 1960 (as amended); Bengali and Bodo are official in Barak Valley and BTR areas respectively.

party_designation.state: State of Assam through the Principal Secretary, Home Department, Government of Assam, Dispur (Guwahati)

verification_format:
I, {deponent_name}, {designation}, do hereby solemnly verify and declare that the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ of the above petition are true to my personal knowledge and the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ are based on information received and legal advice tendered, which I believe to be true. Nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

DEPONENT
localRules: Assamese and English are working languages of the Assam subordinate courts under the Assam Official Language Act, 1960; pleadings before the Gauhati High Court are in English. District court pleadings may be filed in English; Assamese pleadings with English translation are accepted. In Barak Valley districts (Cachar, Karimganj, Hailakandi) Bengali is additionally permitted under the 1961 amendment. In Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR) — Kokrajhar, Chirang, Baksa, Udalguri, Tamulpur — Bodo (Devanagari script) is recognised.

Bail applications under S.483 BNSS (formerly S.439 CrPC) before the Sessions Court must disclose any prior rejection by a Magistrate or co-ordinate court; the application is to be accompanied by a certified copy of the FIR, case diary extract (where available) and the bail order, if any.

Anticipatory bail applications (S.482 BNSS) must be accompanied by an affidavit, certified copy of the FIR and grounds of apprehension. The Gauhati High Court is the preferred forum for AB in serious offences; Sessions Court entertains AB concurrently subject to S.482(4) BNSS.
Vakalatnama in the form prescribed under the Gauhati High Court Rules to be filed at the first instance with requisite court-fee stamp; mofussil districts follow the same form.
All civil pleadings to be paginated, indexed and accompanied by a list of documents under Order VII / Order VIII CPC; verification on affidavit per the Assam High Court (Civil) Rules.
Court-fee under the Court-Fees Act, 1870 as in force in Assam with State amendments (Assam Court-Fees (Amendment) Act); ad valorem fee structure applies to civil suits.

SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, POCSO and NDPS cases are tried by designated Special Courts notified by the State Government — typically the District & Sessions Judge or an Additional Sessions Judge at the district headquarters.

Designated Special Courts also exist for offences under the Assam Land and Revenue Regulation, 1886 (where notified) and the Assam Rifles Act / AFSPA-overlay zones; revenue forums under the Land Revenue Regulation interface with civil jurisdiction.

Sixth Schedule autonomous councils — Bodoland Territorial Council (BTR), Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council, Dima Hasao Autonomous Council — have their own customary courts (Village / Subordinate District Council Courts) under the Assam Autonomous Districts (Administration of Justice) Regulation, 1952; pleadings before regular courts in Karbi Anglong, West Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao must verify which forum has jurisdiction (autonomous council court vs. regular sessions / district court).

Post-2015 reorganisation districts (Charaideo, West Karbi Anglong, Hojai, South Salmara-Mankachar, Biswanath, Majuli) and post-2020 districts (Bajali, Tamulpur) have sessions/district establishments at various stages of full notification — where the local district court is not yet fully constituted, matters are partly heard at the parent district headquarters; advocate must confirm current notification status with the Gauhati High Court Registry before filing.

Border districts (Dhubri, South Salmara-Mankachar, Karimganj) frequently see Foreigners' Tribunal references under the Foreigners (Tribunals) Order, 1964; these are quasi-judicial bodies distinct from the regular courts.
e_filing_note: e-Filing is operational at Guwahati, Dibrugarh, Silchar, Jorhat and select district headquarters via the eCourts portal; not yet mandatory state-wide. The Gauhati High Court has its own e-filing portal.
